subject: SDK conversion lane: pre-launch implementation checklist
messages:
From: Sam Reeves <sam.reeves@lumacare.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Nadia Ortiz <nadia.ortiz@lumacare.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: SDK conversion lane + sandbox requests

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this on. LumaCare is on a tight runway to migrate our inference calls off the legacy endpoint and into Redwood's SDK within the next 3 weeks. We want to run a sandbox pass and a staged cutover. Quick asks so the team can scope work: 

- Can you confirm available sandbox capacity and whether we get a dedicated sandbox model instance?
- We need a recommended retry/backoff matrix and suggested default timeouts for our client lib.
- Will you provide an onboarding sample (Node + Python) that includes token batching guidance?
- Who from Redwood will be our day-to-day technical contact during the integration?

Attached: integration-spec-v1.pdf (pdf) — high level API contract and example payloads.

We can do a 30m sync tomorrow or early next week. Proposed attendees: Nadia (implementation lead), me, our DevOps lead.

Thanks,
Sam Reeves
Head of Integrations
LumaCare
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reeves <sam.reeves@lumacare.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: SDK conversion lane + sandbox requests

Hi Sam — great to meet you over email. I'm the implementation engineer assigned to your migration and will be the primary point for technical questions. Monica (CSM) and Vivek (runtime lead) are on copy for capacity and cutover coordination.

Quick answers up front:
- Sandbox capacity: We can provision a short-lived dedicated sandbox instance for your account for the duration of the smoke tests (typically 2–4 days). We'll need expected concurrency and sample QPS.
- Recommended client defaults (initial):
  - Retries: 3 attempts total (initial=100ms, backoff *2, jitter 0.1–0.2)
  - HTTP timeout: 60s request-level, 30s connection-level
  - Streaming timeout/window: 15s idle (for streaming responses)

I've pasted minimal sample initialization below — we'll update the repo with expanded samples after the sync.

Python (requests-based):
import requests
from redwood_sdk import Client
client = Client(api_key="REDACTED", timeout=60, max_retries=3)
response = client.generate("Hello")

Node (fetch wrapper):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, timeout: 60000, retries: 3 });
await client.generate('Hello');

Proposed next steps: schedule a 30m sandbox-intake call tomorrow 10:30–11:00 PT or Monday 09:00–09:30 PT. Please confirm attendees and expected peak QPS for the tests. I'll also attach a short preflight checklist by EOD.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reeves <sam.reeves@lumacare.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: SDK conversion lane + sandbox requests

Thanks, Sam & Jasmine — adding the CSM handshake and a stepped implementation lane so expectations are clear. High-level implementation commitments (LumaCare -> Redwood):

1) Sandbox prep (Day -3 to Day 0)
  - LumaCare provides sample payloads and expected concurrency (peak QPS, average payload size).
  - Redwood provisions a sandbox model instance and a telemetry hook (temporary API key).

2) Smoke + functional tests (Day 0)
  - Run integration smoke tests against the sandbox instance.
  - Verify token accounting, KV cache behavior (if using streaming/long-context), and latency targets.

3) Cutover rehearsal & staged traffic shift (Day 1–3)
  - Canary 5% traffic for 2 hours, 20% for 6 hours, then full shift if no regressions.
  - Auto-fallback policy in place to redirect to previous endpoint for 30 minutes on error spike.

Implementation checklist (technical) — action owners in parens:
- SDK sample repo (Jasmine): provide Node + Python examples demonstrating batching, backoff and streaming guard rails.
- Retry matrix (Vivek): suggested latency thresholds and 429 handling: backoff with exponential jitter; for 429 escalate to rate-limits@redwood.com if persistent for >5 minutes.
- Timeouts (Jasmine): default timeouts above; client tunables documented.
- Metrics/telemetry (Sam): ensure you can emit request ids for correlation. Provide a mapping to your observability (Datadog/NewRelic).

Sample retry pseudo-code (please copy into your client):
function withRetries(fn) {
  let attempts = 0;
  const max = 3;
  while (attempts < max) {
    try {
      return fn();
    } catch (err) {
      attempts++;
      if (attempts >= max) throw err;
      sleep((100 * Math.pow(2, attempts)) + jitter());
    }
  }
}

Sandbox checklist link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-impl-lane (read-only for LumaCare)

I attached a short preflight spreadsheet and will follow up with a required config list for the production cutover.

-- Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Reeves <sam.reeves@lumacare.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Nadia Ortiz <nadia.ortiz@lumacare.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: SDK conversion lane + sandbox requests

Thanks — that looks good. We can provide sample payloads and expected QPS by EOD today. Sandbox window for us would ideally be next Wednesday (2026-09-09) so we can coordinate internal QA. A couple quick clarifications: 

- For 429 handling: is the recommendation to perform client-side token bucket smoothing (leaky bucket) before retries? We can implement but want to make sure you don't treat client smoothing as substitute for server-side rate-limit config.
- On timeouts: will longer streaming responses (multi-chunk) need a different idle window? We rely on streaming for partial results; want to avoid premature socket closure.

Happy to take the 30m tomorrow 10:30 PT to finalize. Nadia will join for the QA plan.

Sam
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Sam Reeves <sam.reeves@lumacare.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: SDK conversion lane + sandbox requests

Sam — quick answers and confirmation for tomorrow's sync at 10:30 PT.

- 429 handling: yes, implement client-side smoothing (leaky token bucket) to reduce burst retries. That combined with server-side rate limits is recommended. We'll coordinate the exact rate thresholds during the sandbox run — Redwood's rate governor will surface 429s with a Retry-After when appropriate.

- Streaming timeouts: use a longer idle window for streaming clients. Suggested defaults: idle window 30s for long-poll/streaming, send keepalive pings every 10s for long-running responses. We'll include the keepalive examples in the SDK repo.

Attached: preflight-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet) — please fill the 'expected QPS' and 'payload sizes' columns before the call.

For tomorrow: agenda (10:30–11:00 PT)
1) Confirm attendees & sandbox window
2) Share payloads + expected concurrency
3) Run quick sanity test plan and confirm pass/fail criteria
4) Define canary plan for traffic shift

See you tomorrow.

—Jasmine
Implementation Engineer, Redwood Inference
